subject: Retention boundaries: ephemeral tokens, session artifacts, and prompt derivatives
body:
Message 1
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@brightpath.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Q — what exactly is retained by default?

Hi Hannah,

Were kicking off a pilot with Redwood and Legal asked for a compact summary: what Redwood keeps by default for API requests. The specific items they want clarified are:
- Streamed token fragments when we use streaming (are those persisted anywhere?)
- In-session KV cache and whether its stored beyond a single session
- If prompts (user input) vs model outputs are treated differently by default
- Any attachments uploaded as part of a request — do those land in object storage and for how long?

Can you give a short, concrete answer we can share with Legal? If theres a short SLA/TTL table or a runbook we can link, that would be perfect.

Thanks,
Olivia
BrightPath AI

----

Message 2
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@brightpath.ai>
Cc: katarpark_copy@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q — what exactly is retained by default?

Hi Olivia,

Thanks — short version up front, longer details below. You can paste the short version to Legal.

Short answer (copyable):
- By default Redwood persists request metadata and final model outputs.
- Streaming fragments (intermediate token buffers) are ephemeral and are not written to persistent logs unless the customer explicitly enables streaming persistence.
- In-session KV cache is treated as ephemeral session state and is not persisted to long-term storage by default; it exists only for the lifetime of the session instance.
- Prompts (raw user inputs) are treated as part of request metadata and are captured by default unless a customer has an opt-out flag or uses a private deployment mode with different configuration.
- Binary attachments referenced in a request are stored in our object store for a default of 30 days for hosted customers; they are included in retention/deletion workflows and can be excluded via enterprise contracts.

Full detail and practical guidance:
1) What we persist by default
- Request record: request ID, timestamp, headers, and the canonical user prompt text (if provided) are kept to support debugging, billing, and quality monitoring.
- Final outputs: the completed model response(s) are stored because we surface them in the Console and they power evaluation/quality features.

2) What is ephemeral
- Streaming token buffers: we buffer tokens in-memory at the serving tier while a stream is active; these fragments are not checkpointed to long-term storage and are dropped when the stream closes. If a customer opts into "stream-persistence" (a per-route flag), we will atomically persist the final transcript only, not every micro-fragment.
- KV cache: per-session KV cache (model-attention caches) is maintained in-memory/GPU and not written to persistent stores. It is ephemeral by design to protect latent context and to improve performance.

3) Attachments and file artifacts
- Attached files included as request payloads are stored in our object store. Default retention is 30 days for hosted customers; Dedicated and Private customers can configure their own storage TTLs via contract. Attachments are referenced in the request record; deletion obeys the same erasure pathways as request/output records.

4) Deletion pathways and proof of deletion
- Deletion requests from customers trigger an orchestrated erasure flow: logical deletion -> tombstone -> background purge -> storage overwrite where possible.
- We provide deletion evidence (hashes and purge logs) for enterprise customers; for hosted customers we provide a deletion confirmation and the runbook ID.

5) Exceptions and compliance holds
- Legal/Compliance holds (eDiscovery) will suspend purge flows until the hold is released.
- Aggregated telemetry and low-resolution metrics are retained longer for SLO monitoring; those artifacts are non-reversible aggregates and do not contain raw prompts/outputs.

If you want, I can convert the short answer into a 1-page PDF with the TTL table and a bulleted FAQ for your Legal team.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

----

Message 3
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@brightpath.ai>
Date: 2027-03-20T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q — what exactly is retained by default?

Adding a compliance note. Hi Olivia — two clarifications from Compliance:
- Residency: for EU-region customers, attachments and final outputs are stored in-region by default; deletion flows also run in-region.
- Proof-of-deletion: we create a deletion artifact that includes the object IDs removed, the runbook ID, and timestamps. We can produce these artifacts on demand for enterprise customers under NDA.

Also: if BrightPath needs no retention of prompts (i.e., treat prompts as ephemeral), we can set a per-account default flag before your pilot starts and that will prevent prompt text from being written to long-term logs. That flag also removes prompt text from any evaluation exports unless you explicitly opt in.

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

----

Message 4
From: Samir Patel <samir@brightpath.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q — what exactly is retained by default?

Thanks both. Two quick follow-ups so we can close with Legal:
1) If we request "prompt-ephemeral" for our account, how does that affect Console features (are transcripts still visible to users in Console?)
2) For the attachment TTL — is the 30-day default counted from upload time or from last access?

Also wed like to request deletion evidence for a small pilot dataset after the pilot wraps next month. What form does that come in and who do we contact to request it?

— Samir
BrightPath AI

----

Message 5
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightpath.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T14:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q — what exactly is retained by default?

Samir — answers inline:
1) prompt-ephemeral: if enabled, prompts will not be shown in the Console transcript or included in evaluation exports. Session-level debugging still works via request IDs, but the raw user text is redacted. Console features that depend on prompt text (search across prompts, prompt-level quality tags) will be disabled for your account.
2) attachment TTL: default 30 days from upload time. Last access does not reset the TTL. For Dedicated/Private customers TTL is configurable.

Deletion evidence: for your pilot we can provide a short artifact (CSV of object IDs + runbook ID + timestamps + sha256 hashes) and a one-paragraph confirmation note signed by our Compliance lead. Please open a Support ticket titled "Pilot deletion evidence — BrightPath" and tag it with your account ID. Ive attached a one-page summary and a blank proof request form to this thread (stubs).

Action items:
- Olivia/Samir: confirm whether you want prompt-ephemeral for the pilot.
- If yes, well schedule a brief config window (15–30 minutes) and confirm via ticket.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if Legal wants to walk the runbook end-to-end.

Best,
Hannah

Attachments referenced: redwood-retention-summary-stub.pdf, proof-of-deletion-form-stub.docx
